transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-30
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Mikaela Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Evan Morales (Lumos Security Lead), Dr. Sienna Patel (Lumos Head of Engineering), Marcus Lee (Procurement), Tanya Rivera (Compliance)

Auto summary (auto-generated, may be partial): Discussed what evidence is required to get through Lumos' vendor risk questionnaire. Heavy focus on SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logging, KMS and encryption, and where Redwood can provide artifacts and extracts.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call? We have Jordan from Redwood, Priya our solutions engineer, Mikaela on CS, and on the Lumos side who do we have?
[00:10] Evan - Lumos: Evan here, security. Hi.
[00:12] Sienna: Sienna, engineering lead.
[00:14] Marcus: Marcus from procurement.
[00:16] Tanya: Tanya, compliance.
[00:18] Jordan: Great. Goal for today is to walk through the vendor questionnaire and call out where we can provide standard artifacts vs where we need a config or environment-specific extract. We'll also flag any potential gaps. Sound good?
[00:28] Evan: Yep, that's what we need. We're on a tight timeline — we have the vendor board on Oct 20.
[00:32] Jordan: Okay good to know. Priya, do you want to kick to the SIG/CAIQ mapping?
[00:38] Priya (SE): Sure. So first, two quick notes: Redwood maintains a standard SIG mapping and a CAIQ-friendly evidence pack — it's basically a mapping of SIG questions to documents and controls. We can share the spreadsheet and the control references. For SOC 2, our latest report is available to signed NDA partners; it's a point-in-time report but we also have ongoing monitoring artifacts.
[01:02] Evan: When you say "ongoing monitoring artifacts" do you mean logs or like internal controls evidence?
[01:06] Priya: Both — we can provide policy docs, system configuration screenshots, and export samples of audit logs. For production audit logs we usually provide a sanitized sample or an event log extract, not full raw logs.
[01:18] Tanya: On the vendor form they want log retention numbers and proof that logs are immutable. Can you do WORM or append-only evidence?
[01:26] Priya: We don't surface a WORM label per se, but our logging pipeline is write-once append-only and we store tamper-evident indices. We can provide an architecture diagram plus a sample hash-chain proof for events. I will note that the wording may not exactly match a customer's policy so we typically explain the architecture and provide artifact examples.
[01:42] Sienna: For the SOC 2 scope — is it in-scope for data processing and telemetry for hosted or for private deployments too?
[01:50] Jordan: Good question: our SOC 2 covers the Redwood hosted control plane and hosted inference service. For Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) we provide a separate package and a set of technical controls customers can run — the SOC 2 doesn't automatically extend to customer-managed infra. We document that clearly in the mapping.
[02:08] Evan: Okay that distinction is key. Lumos will likely need Private or Dedicated given PHI considerations.
[02:14] Marcus: Our procurement flag is we need clear options for isolated environments and vendor support SLA.
[02:20] Priya: For Dedicated we have SLA options and isolated GPU pools; for Private we have a customer-managed control plane or an appliance. For both we include RBAC and audit logging; for private you can bring your KMS.
[02:32] Evan: About KMS — does Redwood support BYOK and HSM? We need to know for encryption at rest and key separation.
[02:38] Priya: Yes, we support KMS integrations with major cloud KMS providers and a BYOK flow. HSM-backed key stores are supported for Dedicated and Private. For hosted there's a managed KMS option but we can offer an enterprise KMS integration under contract.
[02:56] Tanya: Do you have a diagram or a runbook that shows how keys are rotated and who has access? We need evidence that key rotation exists and that access is limited.
[03:06] Jordan: We can provide the KMS policy doc, rotation schedule, and an access matrix. We'll redact operational usernames. Priya, note to attach KMS rotation policy.
[03:16] Priya: Noted. Also for encryption in transit and at rest we can provide TLS cert chain info and storage encryption details.
[03:24] Evan: Audit logs — retention and access controls. The questionnaire asks: who can read logs, who can delete, is there separation of duty, how long are they kept? Can you provide the retention constants?
[03:36] Priya: By default we retain control plane audit logs for 13 months in hosted. For Dedicated you can configure retention; we recommend minimum 12 months. We enforce RBAC so only security and SRE roles have delete privileges, and deletes are audited and require two-step processes. We can provide an excerpt of access policies and a sample audit entry showing delete protection.
[03:54] Evan: Are those logs stored in a tamper-evident store? Is there an append-only flag?
[03:58] Priya: Yes, architecture uses append-only storage with signed metadata — as I said earlier we can provide hash proofs. There's also an immutable snapshot export we can produce for an audit.
[04:10] Marcus: On the vendor questionnaire under "Data residency" they ask whether data can be restricted to a region and whether backups cross borders. What are Redwood's guarantees?
[04:22] Jordan: We have region controls for hosted — policies allow you to pin data to specific cloud regions and we do not replicate control-plane data outside selected regions without consent. Backups for hosted remain in-region unless you opt into multi-region DR. For Dedicated and Private deployments, you control residency entirely. We'll provide a data residency doc.
[04:40] Sienna: Does that include model weights or embeddings? Because some of our PII ends up in vectors during embedding generation.
[04:48] Priya: Good call — embeddings and model inputs are treated as customer data. For hosted we do not use customer data to train models. For Dedicated and Private the vectors live in customer-controlled stores; we can advise on prefix caching and TTL to limit persistence. We can also configure masking or tokenization pre-ingest if needed.
[05:06] Evan: The questionnaire also asks about SSO — supported protocols, provisioning, SCIM, role mapping. Can you walk through what Redwood supports with an Okta integration?
[05:18] Priya: Sure. We support SAML 2.0 for SSO, OIDC, and SCIM for user provisioning. Role mapping is pluggable: you can map Okta groups to Redwood RBAC roles. For Dedicated/Private we can enable customer SAML endpoints and local IDP configs. For audit we log all auth events with context.
[05:36] Tanya: For role mapping, do you have least-privilege templates? The form asks for an RBAC matrix.
[05:42] Priya: We have default role templates: Admin, Dev, Ops, Viewer, Security. We will send an RBAC matrix doc you can use as a starting point; customers commonly customize it.
[05:52] Jordan: I'll attach the RBAC matrix to the SIG mapping.
[05:56] Marcus: Procurement question — in the event of a breach, what's your notification SLA? The questionnaire asks for incident response time and contacts.
[06:04] Jordan: We have incident response policies and an SLA for customer notification: initial notification within 24 hours for confirmed incidents, with ongoing updates. For high-severity incidents we commit to a faster timeline under enterprise agreements. We'll provide the IR runbook excerpt and contact process.
[06:18] Evan: For evidence items — what are the typical deliverables you can provide without an NDA? We want to pre-fill sections before we sign anything if possible.
[06:28] Priya: Public items: our security whitepaper, architecture diagrams, RBAC matrix template, high-level SOC 2 scope statement, and redacted audit log samples. For the SOC 2 full report we usually require an NDA or IAA. Some customers accept certified attestation summaries first.
[06:44] Sienna: Is there a checklist you can provide mapping each vendor question to an artifact so we know what to paste into the form?
[06:52] Priya: Yes — that's exactly the SIG mapping. We'll populate it with which doc or screenshot satisfies each line. We'll also flag any ambiguous questions that likely need a config-specific extract.
[07:02] Jordan: Quick note — if Lumos decides on Private deployment, we'll still help with a standard mapping but some evidence will need to come from your infra team since it's customer-managed.
[07:12] Evan: Understood. A few technical clarifications from Sienna then: 1) How do you handle KV cache in your runtime and whether caches persist to disk? 2) When streaming tokens, are there any logs that include content that might be PII?
[07:28] Priya: KV cache is in-memory with optional prefix caching; we don't persist raw KV cache to long-term storage unless configured for debugging. For streaming, request/response payloads are logged in a redacted fashion by default; full payload capture is off by default and considered admin-level debug. You can configure retention and redaction rules. We'll provide the request logging policy and an example redact config.
[07:50] Sienna: If we enable a capture for debugging, is that encrypted at rest with customer keys?
[07:55] Priya: Yes, customer-requested captures can be stored encrypted using your KMS if you're on Dedicated or Private. For hosted captures we encrypt with our managed keys unless you have an enterprise KMS set up.
[08:06] Evan: Alright. Marcus, any more procurement points?
[08:09] Marcus: One small one: proof of cyber insurance and sublimit for breach response. That goes in the form too.
[08:16] Jordan: We can provide our certificate of insurance and summary of coverages; we'll include that in the security pack.
[08:22] Tanya: A few questions on evidence format: do you prefer a PDF bundle or link to a secure share for artifacts? We need to know how you'll deliver things for our procurement bucket.
[08:30] Jordan: We usually provide a password-protected zip or a secure share link with restricted access and expiry. For sensitive artifacts we gate on an NDA. We'll follow your procurement team's preference.
[08:40] Evan: For the next call, I'd like a concrete example: a sample audit log extract showing a user role change, a sample SCIM provisioning event, and a sample KMS rotation entry. Can Redwood provide those?
[08:52] Priya: Yes, we can. We'll sanitize PII and timestamps but provide realistic samples. I'll add that to the action items.
[08:59] Jordan: Great. We'll also include a short recording/demo of RBAC flows and how we log role changes. Priya: can you demo that?
[09:06] Priya: Yep, I'll prepare a 10-minute demo for the next session and include the export steps so you can reproduce.
[09:12] Sienna: One more: the questionnaire asks about third-party subprocessor list and vendor management. Can you provide current subprocessors and where contracts are posted?
[09:22] Jordan: We'll include our subprocessors list and a description of the controls we require from them.
[09:28] Evan: Any known compliance gaps relative to healthcare regs HIPAA? I know Redwood positions for enterprise but we need to map it to our PHI requirements.
[09:36] Priya: Redwood is not a HIPAA-covered entity by default; for customers with PHI we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments and will provide BAA language under contract. We'll include a BA/contract template for review.
[09:48] Marcus: Great, that helps.
[09:50] Jordan: Okay let's recap and assign owners. Action items: Jordan to send the security pack, RBAC matrix and insurance cert; Priya to prepare demo and sanitized log extracts; Lumos (Evan/Tanya) to fill initial sections of the form and share regulatory requirements. Any objections?
[10:08] Evan: Sounds good. One question: if we need a POC, can Redwood spin up a short Dedicated trial or do we need to go through procurement?
[10:18] Jordan: We can provision a temporary Dedicated environment for POC — we have a POC flow for procurement-light trials. We'll coordinate with procurement for sign-off but it can be faster than a full contract.
[10:28] Marcus: We'll need pricing estimates for Dedicated baseline and any add-ons like extended retention and KMS BYOK.
[10:36] Jordan: We'll include a high-level estimate in the follow-up, not a formal quote.
[10:40] Sienna: Timeline-wise — can we get the security pack by Oct 2? That gives us a week to prefill before the vendor board.
[10:48] Jordan: Yes, we'll hit Oct 2.
[10:50] Tanya: We'll plan a 60-minute technical evidence session the following week — Oct 6 or 7.
[10:56] Priya: I'll send a Doodle for availability and prep notes for what to bring.
[11:00] Jordan: Perfect. Anything else?
[11:04] Evan: No, thanks all.
[11:06] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the pack and meeting invite.

End of transcript.
